fields.summary: sendInvoicePerEmail fails with MissingMethodException: invalid makeValidContext() call in InvoiceServicesScript.groovy

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents the functions of the product.
issuetype.name: Bug

fields.description:
**Summary**
The `sendInvoicePerEmail` service in
`component://accounting/src/main/groovy/org/apache/ofbiz/accounting/invoice/InvoiceServicesScript.groovy`
fails at runtime with a MissingMethodException because
`DispatchContext.makeValidContext()` is invoked with a single Map argument,
but no such overload exists. Valid signatures are:
  - makeValidContext(String, String, Map)
  - makeValidContext(ModelService, String, Map)

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Trigger the `sendInvoicePerEmail` service (e.g. from the invoice screen's
   "Send per Email" action, which runs it async via the JobQueue).
2. Observe the async job failure in the OFBiz log.

**Expected behaviour**
The invoice email is scheduled and sent via `sendMailFromScreen`.

**Actual behaviour**
Async job fails with:
  groovy.lang.MissingMethodException: No signature of method:
  org.apache.ofbiz.service.DispatchContext.makeValidContext() is applicable
  for argument types: (LinkedHashMap)

**Proposed fix**
Use the 3-argument overload, passing the target service name and the IN mode:

    Map emailParams = dispatcher.getDispatchContext()
            .makeValidContext('sendMailFromScreen', 'IN', ctx)

Patch attached.

**Environment**
OFBiz <your version/branch>, Groovy 5.0.0-alpha-11, JDK 17

fields.summary: order item attribute autoReserve not stored

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents the functions of the product.
issuetype.name: Bug

fields.description:
Creating an order, adding a product, checking 'Auto Reserve', no inventory reservation happens (service reserveStoreInventory is not called).

The problem results from a missing entry in the order_item_attribute table.

component://order/template/entry/cart/ShowCart.ftl 

order_item_attr_autoReserve

attribute is not stored

comments.body:
Hi [~cahein], could you please clarify what kind of reservation you would like to make?

I’m asking because, if you simply want to reserve inventory items when sales orders are placed, you only need to set '{*}Allocate Resource{*}' to '{*}N{*}' in the store configuration (and therefore the 'Auto Reserve' checkbox will not be displayed on the screen where you add products to the order).

If, instead, you want to use the 'Inventory (Supply) Allocation Planning' feature, you need to set 'Allocate Resource' to 'Y'. If you want some insight into this feature, please refer to OFBIZ-10518. To be honest, the ticket description does not fully clarify all aspects of the allocation planning feature. Perhaps [~deepak.nigam], [~surajk], or [~arunpati] could provide more details on the feature and verify if there are bugs to fix.

Best regards

Anahita

The issue came up when i was debugging Errors related to the allocation plan (item) status. Debugging brought me to the org.apache.ofbiz.order.order.OrderServices.java

String autoReserve = OrderReadHelper.getOrderItemAttribute(orderItem, "autoReserve");

Looking into the related table ('order_item_attribute'), there was no entry, regardless of the state of the 'Auto Reserve' checkbox of the add product screen.

As a temporary workaround we changed the OrderService.java to always assume 'autoReserve' to be true.

 

Hope, this helps to clarify the issue.

fields.summary: Handle and resume stale jobs in case of application node(s) running with Auto-scaling enabled

issuetype.description: A task that needs to be done.
issuetype.name: Task

fields.description:
{*}Scenario{*}: 
In an OFBiz environment running with multiple auto-scaling nodes, individual nodes may be restarted, replaced, or terminated due to ASG relaunch, health failure or unexpected node termination. When such a node goes down, the JobSandbox.runByInstanceId still holds the old node's Instance ID, causing the jobs assigned to that node to remain stuck. This prevents other active nodes from re-picking the jobs because the runByInstanceId still points to the inactive node.

{*}Issue{*}:
 * Jobs remain assigned to the old, inactive node.
 * Jobs got stuck as no active node can pick these jobs considered them as owned by the old node (runByInstanceId=oldNode).

*Implementation Plan to address this issue*

{*}Configuration settings{*}. (at the Service-Engine thread pool level)
 * lease-refresh-millis -> 300000 (in millisecs) (every 5 minutes interval)
 * lease-validation-millis -> 480000 (in millisecs) (every 8 minutes interval)
 * lease-expiry-millis -> 600000 (leaseUpdateStamp should not be > 10 minutes from now())

 # A new custom field *leaseUpdatedStamp* will be introduced at the individual job level (JobSandbox.leaseUpdatedStamp) that will tracks last time when the node was still alive and actively processing their jobs.

 # {*}Heartbeat / Lease Renewal{*}: At a configured interval, every node will update the leaseUpdatedStamp with *now()* for the all the jobs it owned.

 # {*}Lease Expiry Validation{*}: All active nodes will periodically validate all the running jobs to ensure if their leaseUpdatedStamp is being updated within the configured threshold.

 # {*}Recover Stale Jobs{*}: While validating the jobs, any job(s) whose leaseUpdatedStamp is not updated within the threshold, the node owning that job is considered as stale/terminated and all the jobs owned by that node will be released.

 # {*}Logic to release stale jobs{*}:
Jobs that are in Queued or Running status having runByInstanceId assigned and leaseUpdatedStamp exceeds threshold will be moved to Pending status with runByInstanceId set as Null. With this, other active nodes will consider such job(s) as available and will pick them for further execution.

*Sample Workflow with Example*
10:00 AM – Node A picks Job X.
10:05 AM – Node A renews its lease for Job X.
10:10 AM – Node A renews the lease again.
10:11 AM – Node A crashes.

Job Poller Recovery Process:

10:08 AM: Lease validation occurs. Node A is still considered active (because the expiry threshold hasn't been reached yet).
10:16 AM: Lease validation runs again. Node A is still considered active (because the expiry threshold hasn't been reached yet).
10:24 AM: Lease validation occurs. Node A is now dead because the expiry threshold (10 minutes) has passed.
The Job Poller will free the job assigned to Node A, and it will now be available for another active node to pick.

Workflow Diagram:

Refer Stale-Jobs-Management (1).png

comments.body:
Hello [~ankit.joshi],

Thanks for this issue.

Your proposal sound good, I propose to improve it with an orchestrator, to reduce request execute on JobSanbox 

We can add an entity JobPoller where each oOFBiz instance record himself on it. At each poll loop an instance update is state as a beat heart and check if an orchestrator is up (if not it takes the role)

OFBiz instance with the orchestrator role check ofbiz instance activity like you propose for the job and if one seems down, update it status and reset job linked.

We can set the JobPoller like :
 * instanceId
 * pollId
 * lastRunnigDate
 * statusId
 * orchestrator
 * terminatedDate

Like this we can reduce the execution time to control activity under 10s without overload the JobSandbox table with check request.
